name: Calicut International Airport
before:
The airport for Kozhikode in Kerala, known locally as Karipur. It is at Karippur in Malappuram, 28 km from the city, and it is an operating base for Air India Express.

One thing worth flagging before quoting: this is a tabletop runway, one of only a few in India.

Getting to the city is easy enough by road. The airport sits between two national highways, NH-966 just over 2 km away and NH-66 about 8 km away, with good onward connections north to Kannur and Wayanad and south to Malappuram, Palakkad, Thrissur and Coimbatore. Kerala State Road Transport runs an air conditioned FlyBus into Kozhikode, which is the cheapest way in, though there are only a handful of services. Pre-paid taxis, Uber and Ola all serve the terminal.

The airport opened in April 1988 and took international status in February 2006. It matches Hyderabad for international traffic.
after:
The airport for Kozhikode in Kerala, also known as Karipur Airport. It stands 28 km from the city at Karipur in Malappuram district, and Air India Express flies from here.

The runway is a tabletop.

It opened in April 1988 and was declared an international airport in February 2006.

claims.why: Wrong. AAI's international passenger table gives Kozhikode 2,920,143 for April 2025 to March 2026 against Hyderabad's 5,463,102 (and 2,965,957 against 5,048,572 in 2024-25), so it carries a little over half Hyderabad's international traffic. No like-for-like replacement has two sources (see the held-back total below).

claims.why: Held back: a verified total that replaces nothing in the old text, which gave no passenger figure. AAI's table gives 3,855,618 passengers for April 2025 to March 2026 (up 4.3 per cent on 3,695,944), and Wikipedia's infobox gives the same. Of those, 2,920,143 were international (AAI alone), so roughly three in four passengers fly abroad, but that share has only one source.
